threads.title: Design system tokens
threads.preview: Naming scheme for spacing and color

turns.text: Should spacing tokens be named by size or by role?

turns.reasoning: Both approaches are common. Recommend a two-layer scheme so the team gets stable role names without losing raw sizes.
turns.text: Use both, in two layers. Keep a raw scale (space-1 through space-12) and put role tokens on top of it (space-inline, space-stack, space-section). Components reference roles, so a scale change never touches component code.
What is the safest order to migrate sessions to short-lived tokens?

turns.reasoning: Migration needs a dual-read period. Outline steps that let the old and new paths coexist before cutting over.
turns.text: Issue both for a release, read both, then stop issuing the old one. Start by adding token issuance next to the existing session write, make every auth check accept either, and only after a full expiry window remove the session path.

threads.title: Heat pump research
threads.preview: Payback math on replacing a gas boiler

turns.text: How do heat pumps keep working when it's freezing outside?

turns.reasoning: Explain the physics briefly: refrigerant boiling point is far below freezing, so there is still heat to extract. Give one concrete efficiency figure at a cold temperature.
turns.text: Even freezing air holds heat. A heat pump's refrigerant boils far below 0 °C, so it can absorb outdoor heat, compress it to raise the temperature, and release it inside. Modern cold-climate units keep 250–300% efficiency at −15 °C.
Is it worth replacing a gas boiler mid-life?

turns.reasoning: This depends on the price ratio between electricity and gas, the remaining boiler life, and rebates. Give the rule of thumb and the three inputs.
turns.text: Usually yes, if your electricity-to-gas price ratio is under about 3.5. The math hinges on three numbers: your boiler's remaining life, local energy prices, and available rebates. Start with the rebates — in many regions they cover 30–40% of the install, which shortens payback to 6–8 years.

threads.title: SQL for churn cohort
threads.preview: Window function draft, not yet run

turns.text: Write a query that groups users by signup month and shows how many are still active 90 days later.

turns.reasoning: Cohort by signup month, then join activity at day 90. Keep it to one CTE so it is easy to read.
turns.text: Group by date_trunc of the signup date, then left join an activity subquery filtered to events within 90 days of signup. Count distinct users in both, and divide for the retention rate. I drafted it with a single CTE so you can swap the window without touching the join.

turns.text: One of the best. Days sit around 22 °C, the summer crowds are gone, and the sea is still warm enough to swim. Pack a light layer for evenings and expect a few short showers late in the month.
Give me a three-part outline for a quarterly report to the board.

turns.reasoning: Boards want results, then risks, then asks. Map the three sections to that order.
turns.text: Results first, then risks, then asks. Open with the three numbers that moved and why, follow with the two things that could go wrong next quarter, and close with the decisions you need from the board. Keep each section to one page.

threads.title: Dockerfile multi-stage build
threads.preview: Trim the final image below 100 MB

turns.text: Why is my Node image 1.2 GB?

turns.reasoning: Most likely a single-stage build carrying dev dependencies and the full base image. Recommend a multi-stage build on a slim base.
turns.text: You are shipping the build toolchain. Build in one stage on the full image, then copy only the output and production node_modules into a second stage based on node:slim or distroless. That alone usually lands under 150 MB.
What makes a product name easy to remember?

turns.reasoning: Keep to the practical rules: short, easy to spell after hearing it once, and not already crowded.
turns.text: Two syllables, spellable after hearing it once, and no existing product in the same space with a similar sound. Say the name out loud in a sentence and see if you have to explain it.
How do I tell if an index is bloated?

turns.reasoning: Point to pgstattuple for a real measurement, and give the rough threshold where REINDEX pays off.
turns.text: Install pgstattuple and check the leaf fragmentation and free space of the index. Anything above about 30% free space on a hot index is worth a REINDEX CONCURRENTLY. VACUUM alone will not shrink it.
My cover letter is a full page. What should I cut?

turns.reasoning: Most cover letters repeat the resume. Cut everything that is already there and keep the one story that is not.
turns.text: Cut anything the resume already says. Keep one short story that shows how you work, one sentence on why this company, and a plain closing line. That is half a page.
Why does the compiler want a lifetime on this function returning a reference?

turns.reasoning: The function takes two references and returns one; the compiler cannot know which input the output borrows from. Explain elision rules briefly.
turns.text: Because the function takes two references and returns one, the compiler cannot tell which input the result borrows from. A lifetime annotation is you telling it. With a single reference input it would be inferred automatically.
